<!--
Measured, not read: a figure or table on the same page as text stands a
double-spaced blank line clear of it, above and below. "If text appears on
the same page as a table or figure, add a double-spaced blank line between
the text and the table or figure so that the separation between the text and
table or figure is easier to see" (APA, on the manuscript and the student
paper).

The .pdf gave a table that blank line, and a figure in an [H] float about
half of one below and none above. typst gave neither a blank line: one line
from the text to the number, and one from the note to the text below. Both
now set 48pt from the last line of text to the number and from the note to
the next line of text.

The table is set flush left, as APA sets one, and its note on the next line
under its rule. The .pdf centred a markdown table, as longtable does by
default, and stood its note a line and a half under the last row, with
longtable's own \LTpost and half an em on top of the line spacing.

In .docx the blank lines are space before: before a FigureTitle, and
before whatever follows a float. A paragraph after one takes it in its own
style (AfterWithoutNote); a heading or list after one is preceded by a spacer
a point high that carries it, as after the last table below; another float
needs none, its title having the space already. Not space after the float's
note or picture, which Word would add to the next float's space before.

The number is set in bold, which pdftools boxes a point or two taller than
the roman around it, so the space above is measured to the caption, a line
below the number: 72pt.
-->
